commits.message:
fix(comm): stop publishing comm-gateway 8080 directly, externalize RabbitMQ credentials

comm-gateway was published as 8080:8080, exposing it on the public
interface in addition to the intended path through jobfynder-npm
(443, TLS-terminated). Anyone could bypass TLS entirely and hit the
app over plain HTTP. Confirmed both containers share the
communication_default bridge network -- npm resolves comm-gateway:8080
internally without any host port publish, so the mapping was pure
unnecessary exposure, not a functional dependency. Removed. Verified:
direct :8080 access now refuses (000/connection error), public
https://comm.jobfynder.com/health still 200.

RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER/PASS were hardcoded directly in this file,
including a literal CHANGE_THIS_STRONG_PASSWORD placeholder that was
apparently never actually changed -- committed to git in plaintext
across multiple prior commits. Not externally exploitable today (the
management port was never published to the host, confirmed via
docker port), but a real weak/default credential nonetheless. Now
sourced from .env (not committed) via env_file + variable substitution,
same pattern as comm-gateway. Rotated to a new random value via
rabbitmqctl change_password against the live container (does not
require a volume wipe -- RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER/PASS only take effect
on a fresh Mnesia database, so changing the env var alone would not
have rotated the actual live credential).

Not addressed: the old placeholder password remains visible in this
repo's git history on earlier commits. Rotating it makes that
historical value inert, but a full history rewrite (git filter-branch/
BFG) was not attempted here -- disruptive to other clones/collaborators,
out of scope for this fix, flagged as a decision for whoever owns this
repo if a full scrub is wanted.
